Python

Source: vignettes/articles/python.Rmd
python.Rmd

The binning, the statistics and the array assembly are src/, compiled into both languages and answering to the representation contract. window_matrix() here and window_matrix() in R return the same numbers from the same input, and the fixtures under inst/spec/fixtures/ hold them to it.

pip install git+https://github.com/gcol33/climgrain
import climgrain as tg

x = tg.window_matrix(readings, id="plot", time="t", value="temp",
                     window="week", stats=("cold_day", "mean", "warm_day"))
lad = tg.window_ladder(x, y, learners=[tg.mlp_learner(), tg.cnn_learner()])

The contract’s last section says what each language carries, so a difference between the two is a recorded decision.

The pages

The representation

Readings in long form to the array a model is fitted on, at one grain or at every grain of a ladder.

The split and the cells

One fold map read by everything that scores, and the cells a score is defined on, computed with no model involved.

Fitting

Fitting one learner at one grain, fitting every grain of a ladder, and reading the grain a ladder saturates at.

Learners

The arms that ship, and the interface a learner of your own goes through.

Scoring and comparison

The metrics, the paired contrast between two learners on matched cells, and the inflation of a score read at its own best threshold.

Extending

The response head and the metric are registrations, never a fork of the fitting code.

What crosses the boundary

The three artifacts a split is carried in, and the digest that says two arrays are the same array.
